island: Minjerribah / North Stradbroke Island, Quandamooka Country, Queensland, Australia
about: The civic machine of Minjerribah as a policy graph. Institutions, the instruments that bind them, the constituencies that react, the metrics that move, and the levers that move them. The design point is that almost nothing here is the player's to decide alone. This island is governed by a council whose seat also covers a mainland suburb, a state government two departments deep, a Commonwealth whose environment law, native title law and grant programs reach it without anybody in Canberra ever coming over, a Registered Native Title Body Corporate with determined native title over the whole island, a jointly managed national park, and three private transport operators. A player who wants a thing must usually persuade somebody else to do it.
honesty: No lever here is a promise that a system implements it. This is content, not code.
Where a real plan, budget line or statute exists, it is cited. Where a lever is a modelling construct with no current proposal behind it, status says so and confidence is low.
Every cost is an estimate unless a published figure is cited, and published figures carry the year they were published. Construction costs on an island move fast.
Magnitudes are modelling values on a shared scale. They are not measured elasticities. Nobody has given this project measured elasticities for this island.
who_decides is the most important field in the file. It is deliberately, frequently, not the player.

Every institution carries a tier. Counting bodies makes a long list; counting tiers says how hard a thing is, because a lever that needs the council and the state and the Commonwealth needs three governments to agree and a lever that needs the council needs one.

The Commonwealth is a decider on very few levers and a constraint on many. Adding it to who_decides where it does not hold the decision would be as wrong as leaving it out where it does, so most of its weight in this pack sits in instruments rather than in levers.
Ferry, barge, bus and parking capacity numbers belong in data/transport.json, not here. This pack references them and does not restate them.
Nothing cultural is generated here. QYAC appears as a civic and corporate actor with sourced public functions and nothing more.

confidence_scale.high: A named public source states this directly, or it is a matter of public record such as a statute or a determination.
confidence_scale.medium: A credible public source supports it but the figure, date or scope may have moved, or it is inferred from two sources that agree.
confidence_scale.low: Plausible and useful for the simulation, but not verified. Do not show it to a player as fact.

field_guide.institutions[].tier: commonwealth | state | local | native_title | joint | private | none. Which order of government or kind of body it is. A lever's difficulty is derived from how many distinct tiers appear in its who_decides, which is a different and more useful number than how many bodies appear.
field_guide.levers[].id: stable slug, safe as a key
field_guide.levers[].who_decides: one or more institution ids from this file's institutions list. The decision maker, not the funder and not the lobbyist.
field_guide.levers[].player_role: player_decides | player_funds | player_advocates | player_observes. The honest answer to 'can I just do this'.
field_guide.levers[].status: in_place | funded | proposed | under_study | modelled_option | contested. modelled_option means nobody has actually proposed it and this pack invented the framing, not the facts.
field_guide.levers[].cost_aud: capital is a one-off in A$; recurring_per_year is ongoing in A$; basis says where the number came from.
field_guide.levers[].lead_time_months: from decision to the effect starting to appear, not to ribbon cutting.
field_guide.levers[].effects[]: {target, magnitude, delay_months, confidence}. target is a metric id from this file's metrics list.
field_guide.levers[].effects[].magnitude: signed, -1 to +1, as a fraction of that metric's plausible full swing on this island. +0.1 is a real but modest shift. +0.6 is transformative. Sign is in the metric's own units, so a positive magnitude on a metric whose direction is 'lower_is_better' is a worsening.
field_guide.levers[].side_effects[]: second-order consequences a player should be able to discover rather than be told. Same shape as effects plus a description.
field_guide.levers[].who_supports / who_opposes: interest_group ids. Empty is allowed and means genuinely nobody organised cares much.
field_guide.interest_groups[].size: share of the island's civic weight, 0 to 1, across residents plus the non-resident groups that show up to consultation. The set does not sum to 1 because people belong to several groups at once and because visitors are not residents.
field_guide.interest_groups[].base_mood: -1 furious to +1 delighted, at the pack's baseline state with no levers pulled.
field_guide.metrics[].baseline: the value the simulation should start from. index means a 0 to 1 modelling index with no published measurement behind it.
field_guide.metrics[].direction: higher_is_better | lower_is_better | context. context means the value is neither good nor bad on its own.

source_registry.brief: Task brief supplied by the author, not independently verified

jurisdiction.summary: Three townships, one council division shared with a mainland suburb, roughly half the island in a jointly managed national park, native title determined over the whole island in 2011 under Commonwealth law, half the island inside an internationally listed wetland that Commonwealth environment law protects, and every road on and off the island in somebody else's hands.

tiers.note: Four orders of authority reach this island, plus the bodies that are not government at all. A lever's difficulty is how many of these have to agree, not how many names are on it.
tiers.governments_note: Three of the seven tiers are orders of government in the ordinary sense, and counting how many of those three a lever needs is the honest measure of how hard it is. The other four are a native title body corporate, a joint arrangement, private parties and nobody, and each is hard in its own way rather than in that way.

layers.covers: National environment law over the Ramsar wetland that takes in the island's western flats and its perched lakes, the listed threatened and migratory species on them, cetaceans in Commonwealth waters, the Native Title Act under which the 2011 determination was made and the ILUAs registered, telecommunications and postal service obligations, aviation safety and the airspace, biosecurity at the national border, and grant programs that mostly arrive through the state or the council rather than directly.
layers.why_it_matters: Nobody from the Commonwealth sits in a room on this island, and it still holds a veto over the mainland ferry terminal the island depends on. That is what a fourth tier looks like from here.

layers.covers: Roads in the townships, waste, water and wastewater through Redland Water, parks and foreshore, local laws including dogs and camping on council land, the planning scheme, rates.
One councillor. Division 2 covers Cleveland on the mainland and North Stradbroke Island together, so the island's representative also answers to a mainland suburb with far more voters.
layers.why_it_matters: This single fact shapes every island grievance about being outvoted.

layers.covers: The statute that ended mining, the transition funding, national park, marine park, coastal management, planning appeals, health, schools, police, public transport contracts.

Determined native title over Minjerribah since 4 July 2011, the ILUAs that set how those rights are exercised, joint management of the national park, and the island's camping and vehicle access business.
Naree Budjong Djara National Park and the Minjerribah Recreation Area, jointly managed by QYAC and QPWS under an Indigenous Management Agreement.

layers.layer: Private operators on a public function
layers.covers: The vehicle barge and a passenger service between Cleveland and Dunwich. Commercial pricing, commercial timetable, no ballot, no resident quota published.

institutions.label: Redland City Council
institutions.role: Roads, parks, foreshore, waste, water and wastewater, planning scheme, local laws, rates. The island is one part of a city whose population is overwhelmingly on the mainland.

institutions.label: Division 2 councillor
institutions.role: The island's single voice in the council chamber, in a division that also covers Cleveland on the mainland.
institutions.note: The pack deliberately does not name the sitting councillor. Names change; the structure does not.

institutions.label: Redland Water
institutions.role: Reticulated water and the sewerage network in the townships, and the Point Lookout wastewater treatment plant.

institutions.label: Seqwater
institutions.role: Bulk water for the island townships, drawn from bores and treated at small local plants. The island is not on the South East Queensland Water Grid.

institutions.label: Queensland Government
institutions.role: The statute that ended mining, the transition funding, the national park, coastal and marine management, planning appeals, health, schools, police, public transport contracts.

institutions.label: Department of the Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation
institutions.role: Administers Minjerribah Futures and holds the parks and environment functions. The department has been renamed and restructured more than once during the transition, which the audit office found disrupted the program.

institutions.label: Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service
institutions.role: Joint manager of Naree Budjong Djara National Park and the Minjerribah Recreation Area with QYAC.

institutions.label: Joint management, QYAC and QPWS
institutions.role: Indigenous Joint Management Areas run under an Indigenous Management Agreement. Fire, pests, weeds, cultural heritage, assets and visitor management on park.
institutions.note: For any lever on park, this is the decision maker, not the council and not the player.

institutions.label: Quandamooka Yoolooburrabee Aboriginal Corporation
institutions.role: Holds and manages the native title rights and interests of the Quandamooka People recognised on 4 July 2011. Joint manager of the national park. Operator of Minjerribah Camping. Around 550 members, the largest membership of any prescribed body corporate in Australia.
institutions.capacity_note: The Queensland Audit Office found QYAC was assigned multiple complex construction projects at once, with fewer than 100 staff, without an adequate capacity assessment. Capacity is a real constraint in this simulation, not a slur.

institutions.label: Minjerribah Camping
institutions.role: Runs the island's camping grounds and issues the vehicle access permits for the Minjerribah Recreation Area, including Main Beach and Flinders Beach.

institutions.label: Transport and Main Roads, TransLink
institutions.role: Contracts the island bus services and sets the fare policy that applies to them.

institutions.label: Bay Island Transit Systems
institutions.role: Runs island bus routes 880 between Dunwich and Point Lookout and 881 between One Mile, Dunwich and Amity Point, under the TransLink contract at the 50 cent fare.

institutions.label: Economic Development Queensland
institutions.role: Administers the Toondah Harbour Priority Development Area on the mainland side, which contains the vehicle ferry terminal the island depends on.

institutions.label: SeaLink South East Queensland
institutions.role: Vehicle barge and passenger service, Cleveland to Dunwich.

institutions.label: Stradbroke Flyer Gold Cat
institutions.role: Passenger water taxi, Cleveland to One Mile at Dunwich. A second operator on the same crossing.

institutions.label: Sibelco Australia
institutions.role: Ran the island's sand mining to its close and signed a rehabilitation agreement in December 2019 committing to work with QYAC on restoring and surrendering former mining land.

institutions.label: Private landowners
institutions.role: At Amity Point, owners of land behind the central reach of the foreshore carry the construction and maintenance cost of works that protect their own property.

institutions.label: Australian Government
institutions.role: The Commonwealth. It makes the law under which native title over this island was determined and the island's land use agreements were registered, it protects the Ramsar wetland and the listed species on it under national environment law, it sets telecommunications, postal and aviation obligations, it holds biosecurity at the national border, and it pays for things here through programs. It has no office on the island and no officer who lives here.
institutions.seats_on_island: None. The island sits in a federal electorate whose voters are overwhelmingly on the mainland, which is the same shape of problem as Division 2 one tier down.
institutions.money_note: Almost no Commonwealth money reaches this island as a cheque from Canberra. Financial assistance grants are paid to Queensland and passed to the council on the state grants commission's recommendation, disaster funding is jointly funded and administered by the Queensland Reconstruction Authority, and the transition program that reshaped this island is a state program. The Commonwealth is more often the condition on a decision than the maker of one.

institutions.label: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
institutions.role: Administers the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999. A person proposing an action likely to have a significant impact on a matter of national environmental significance refers it, and the environment minister decides whether it is a controlled action and, if it is, whether to approve it and on what conditions. This is the one Commonwealth decision that has already landed on this island's front door.
institutions.note: The pack deliberately does not name the sitting minister. Ministers and department names change; the decision does not. The department has been renamed more than once, which is why the Act is cited rather than the letterhead.
institutions.capacity_note: The referral decision under section 75 runs to a statutory clock of twenty business days. Everything after it does not: a controlled action goes to an assessment that is measured in seasons, and the Toondah referral sat with the Commonwealth from 2018 to 2024.

institutions.label: No formal decision maker
institutions.role: Some things on this island happen because volunteers do them, or do not happen because nobody is left to. Used where a lever has no institutional owner.
institutions.note: The Amity Point Progress Association has wound up, so Amity Point has no local progress association to consult.

instruments.label: North Stradbroke Island Protection and Sustainability Act 2011
instruments.what_it_does: Set the framework for phasing out sand mining on the island. Amended in 2016 to bring the end date back to the end of 2019.
instruments.why_it_matters: It is the reason the island has an economy in transition rather than a mine.

instruments.label: Quandamooka People #1 and #2 determination
instruments.what_it_does: Recognised native title over 54,408 hectares: 2,264 hectares exclusive possession, 22,639 hectares onshore non-exclusive, 29,505 hectares offshore non-exclusive. Delaney on behalf of the Quandamooka People v State of Queensland [2011] FCA 741.

instruments.label: The Quandamooka Indigenous Land Use Agreements
instruments.what_it_does: Two agreements setting how native title rights and interests are exercised on the ground, including the joint management arrangements. The Quandamooka and State of Queensland ILUA was registered by the National Native Title Tribunal on 8 December 2011.
instruments.gap: The full text and the specific schedules that govern camping, tourism and land dealings were not read for this pack.

instruments.label: Naree Budjong Djara management plan
instruments.what_it_does: Sets how QYAC and QPWS jointly manage the national park and the visitor experience within it. Naree Budjong Djara means My Mother Earth.

instruments.label: North Stradbroke Island Economic Transition Strategy
instruments.what_it_does: The original transition package, 23 projects, designed to move the island off sand mining.

instruments.label: Minjerribah Futures
instruments.what_it_does: The successor program to the transition strategy. Approved funding rose from an initial $20 million to $39.4 million as at 30 April 2024, of which $30.6 million had been spent. $8.74 million went directly to QYAC between July 2016 and December 2021.
instruments.audit_findings: The strategy assumed $36.6 million in private investment that never arrived, which forced the state to raise its own contribution. Governance was found to be complex and inconsistent, with inadequate community oversight.

instruments.label: Gumpi (Dunwich) Master Plan
instruments.what_it_does: Sets future residential, commercial, community, environmental and industrial land uses at Dunwich, infrastructure upgrades and the gateway role. A temporary local planning instrument covered 25 land parcels across Gumpi, Pulan Pulan and Mulumba.
instruments.gap: Whether the master plan has been given effect in the current Redland City Plan was not confirmed.

instruments.label: Amity Point Shoreline Erosion Management Plan
instruments.what_it_does: A 20 year plan splitting the Amity Point foreshore into three reaches. Northern reach: surveys and coastal process studies. Central reach: formalising and maintaining the rock flow slide barrier. Southern reach: a buried seawall and sand nourishment.

instruments.label: Coastal Hazard Adaptation Strategy
instruments.what_it_does: A 20 to 100 year plan for erosion, sea level rise and storm tide across the whole city coastline. The 2016 current hazards phase identified Amity Point as the only area at high risk of coastal erosion.

instruments.label: Declared erosion prone area
instruments.what_it_does: Amity Point is a declared erosion prone area under the Coastal Protection and Management Act 1995, which constrains what can be built and where.

instruments.label: Quandamooka water reserves
instruments.what_it_does: Established two water reserves totalling 61,190 megalitres for the Quandamooka People, split evenly between environmental and cultural use and economic use and land rehabilitation, from water previously allocated to sand mining.

instruments.label: Sibelco rehabilitation agreement
instruments.what_it_does: Commits Sibelco to work with QYAC on rehabilitating and surrendering former mining land on the island.

instruments.label: Toondah Harbour Priority Development Area
instruments.what_it_does: The mainland end of the island's vehicle ferry link, declared a Priority Development Area in 2013. The private development partner withdrew its federal application in April 2024, days after the federal environment minister announced a proposed refusal. As reported in April 2026, the Priority Development Area remains in place but has no private sector partner and the redevelopment pathway is unclear.
instruments.why_it_matters: The island's front door on the mainland has no development partner and no settled plan. Every access lever runs through this uncertainty. The withdrawn proposal had included a new ferry terminal, so the terminal upgrade went with it.

instruments.label: Redland Local Housing Action Plan
instruments.what_it_does: Council's housing actions, which record that businesses on the island struggle to recruit because there is nowhere for workers to live, and that the island housing co-operative had no vacancies across its portfolio.
instruments.gap: The plan PDF returned 403 to this agent and was read only through search result extracts. Figures should be checked against the document itself.

instruments.label: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999
instruments.the_part_that_bites: Part 3, the matters of national environmental significance. Section 16 for a declared Ramsar wetland, section 18 for a listed threatened species or ecological community, section 20 for a listed migratory species, section 23 for a Commonwealth marine area. Part 7 is the referral, section 75 is the decision on whether an action is a controlled action, and Part 9 is the approval.
instruments.what_it_does: Makes it an offence to take an action that has, will have or is likely to have a significant impact on one of the matters of national environmental significance without the environment minister's approval. The proponent refers the action, the minister has twenty business days to decide whether it is a controlled action, and a controlled action is then assessed and approved, approved with conditions, or refused.
instruments.why_it_matters: This island carries at least four of those matters at once, and the twin already simulates two of them without ever saying whose law they belong to: the western sand flats where the eastern curlew and the bar-tailed godwit roost, and the koala habitat the planning overlay argues about. The Act does not manage the island. It sits over anybody who wants to do something to it.
instruments.gap: The section numbers are as the Act stands on the public consolidations cited. No legal advice was taken and no referral for anything on this island was read.

instruments.label: Moreton Bay Ramsar site
instruments.the_part_that_bites: EPBC Act section 16, which is what turns an international listing into an Australian offence.
instruments.what_it_does: Listed under the Ramsar Convention on 22 October 1993, covering over 120,000 hectares of Moreton Bay and taking in North Stradbroke Island. Australia's obligation is to maintain the site's ecological character and to report any change in it.
instruments.quote: The Ramsar site is home to nationally threatened plant species that are wetland dependent, such as the endangered swamp daisy, Olearia hygrophila, which is only found on North Stradbroke Island.
instruments.why_it_matters: Half of this island is inside an internationally listed wetland and nothing in this pack said so until now. It is also the reason the mainland ferry terminal proposal failed: the minister's proposed refusal turned on removing 58.7 hectares from the Ramsar site.
instruments.gap: The Queensland fact sheet cited is dated 2013, so its figures are as at that date. The precise cadastral boundary is in the Commonwealth boundary description, which was not read for this pack, so this record does not state which parts of the island are inside the line.

instruments.label: Japan and Australia Migratory Bird Agreement
instruments.what_it_does: Signed 6 February 1974 and in force from 30 April 1981. Commits both countries to cooperate on conserving the migratory birds that move between them, and lists those species in an annex.
instruments.the_part_that_bites: A bird on the annex is a listed migratory species under the EPBC Act, so section 20 applies to any action likely to have a significant impact on it.
instruments.why_it_matters: The birds on the flats off Dunwich and Amity Point are on that annex. A treaty signed in Tokyo is the reason a dog off its lead at a high-tide roost is a national matter and not only a local one.

instruments.label: China and Australia Migratory Bird Agreement
instruments.parties: Australia and the People's Republic of China
instruments.what_it_does: Signed 20 October 1986 and in force from 1 September 1988. The same shape as JAMBA: cooperation on the conservation of birds that migrate between the two countries, with the species named in an annex.
instruments.the_part_that_bites: EPBC Act section 20, through the listing of annex species as listed migratory species.
instruments.why_it_matters: The Yellow Sea staging grounds these birds depend on are the pressure the shorebird model already names as beyond any island lever. This is the instrument through which that pressure is anybody's business at all.

instruments.label: Republic of Korea and Australia Migratory Bird Agreement
instruments.parties: Australia and the Republic of Korea
instruments.what_it_does: The third of the three bilateral migratory bird agreements, with the same structure and the same annex mechanism.
instruments.why_it_matters: Three treaties, four countries, and a consultative meeting every two years, all of it reaching a sand flat you can walk onto from a caravan park.
instruments.gap: The signature and entry-into-force dates for ROKAMBA were not confirmed to the same standard as JAMBA and CAMBA, so only the year is stated.

instruments.label: Australian Whale Sanctuary
instruments.the_part_that_bites: EPBC Act section 225, with the offences in Part 13 Division 3.
instruments.what_it_does: Establishes a sanctuary covering the Commonwealth marine area, which begins beyond the three nautical mile limit of state coastal waters and runs out to the edge of the exclusive economic zone. Inside it, killing, injuring, taking, harassing, chasing or herding a cetacean is an offence without a permit.
instruments.why_it_matters: The humpbacks the twin puts past Point Lookout between June and October swim across a jurisdictional line nobody can see. Inshore of it Queensland's rules apply; outside it the Commonwealth's do. It is the clearest example on this island of authority defined by a distance from a baseline rather than by a fence.
instruments.gap: Where exactly the three nautical mile line falls off Point Lookout was not established for this pack, and no approach distance for whale watching is stated here. Queensland sets those in state waters and this pack does not restate them.

instruments.label: The Offshore Constitutional Settlement
instruments.the_part_that_bites: Coastal Waters (State Powers) Act 1980 and Coastal Waters (State Title) Act 1980, in force from 1982 and 1983.
instruments.what_it_does: Divides authority over the sea between the Commonwealth and the states. The states hold powers and title in coastal waters out to three nautical miles from the territorial sea baseline. Beyond that is the Commonwealth marine area.
instruments.why_it_matters: Every marine argument on this island, the marine park, the fisheries closures, the whale approaches, sits on one side of that line or the other, and the pack had no record of where the line is or who drew it.

instruments.label: Native Title Act 1993
instruments.the_part_that_bites: Section 223 defines native title, section 225 is what a determination determines, sections 56 and 57 require the Federal Court to determine a prescribed body corporate to hold or manage the rights, Part 2 Division 3 Subdivision C is the area agreement, and section 199A is the Register of Indigenous Land Use Agreements the Native Title Registrar keeps.
instruments.what_it_does: The Commonwealth law under which the Quandamooka determinations of 4 July 2011 were made, under which QYAC exists as a registered native title body corporate, and under which the island's land use agreements were registered.
instruments.why_it_matters: Fourteen levers in this pack name QYAC as a decision maker and none of them named the law that makes that so. QYAC's standing here is not a courtesy and not a consultation arrangement. It is a Commonwealth statute and a Federal Court determination.
instruments.note: This record names the machinery and nothing else. It records no view of QYAC's, describes no content of any agreement, and the two ILUAs remain unread. See the existing instrument iluas-2011 and docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md B16.

instruments.label: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act 1984
instruments.the_part_that_bites: Section 9 for an emergency declaration and section 10 for other declarations, both made by the Commonwealth minister on application by or on behalf of Aboriginal people, where the minister is satisfied an area is a significant Aboriginal area under threat of injury or desecration.
instruments.what_it_does: Gives a Commonwealth minister the power to declare protection for an area or an object, which can override a state approval.
instruments.why_it_matters: It is recorded here as a mechanism that exists and can be invoked, because a governance model of an Australian place that leaves it out is incomplete. That is the whole of its presence in this project.
instruments.handling_rule: BLOCKING. This project models no application under this Act, no declaration, no area, no site and no threat, and it holds no location. Nothing about it is a lever, a mechanic, an outcome or an event. Naming the Act is a fact about Australian law. Anything beyond naming it would be this project speculating about Quandamooka cultural heritage, which data/lore.json forbids and which is QYAC's alone. Do not model it.

instruments.label: The statutory infrastructure provider regime
instruments.the_part_that_bites: Part 19 of the Telecommunications Act 1997, in force from 1 July 2020.
instruments.what_it_does: Makes NBN Co the default statutory infrastructure provider for Australia, and obliges the provider for an area, on request from a retail service provider, to connect premises and supply a wholesale service capable of at least 25 megabits per second down and 5 up, over fixed line where that is reasonable and over fixed wireless or satellite where it is not.
instruments.why_it_matters: The obligation is to connect a premises on request. It is not an obligation to cover a road, a beach or a headland, which is why the twin's telecoms model can carry dead spots on an island where every house can get a service.
instruments.gap: Which technology serves each township on Minjerribah was not established for this pack. No claim is made about what any island address can actually get.

instruments.label: Australia Post community service obligations
instruments.the_part_that_bites: Section 27 of the Australian Postal Corporation Act 1989.
instruments.what_it_does: Requires Australia Post to supply a letter service, to make it reasonably accessible to all people in Australia on an equitable basis wherever they live, to meet performance standards that reasonably meet the community's social, industrial and commercial needs, and to charge a single uniform rate for a standard letter anywhere in Australia.
instruments.why_it_matters: It is the reason a letter to a house at Amity Point costs what a letter across a Brisbane suburb costs, on an island where everything else arrives by barge at a freight rate. One of the very few things here that is deliberately not priced by distance.
instruments.gap: Nothing here states what mail service the island actually receives, how often, or through which outlet. The obligation is on the record; the local arrangement is not.

instruments.label: Aviation safety regulation, and an uncertified strip
instruments.the_part_that_bites: The Civil Aviation Act 1988 and the Civil Aviation Safety Regulations. Part 139 of those regulations sets the standards for certified aerodromes, and it does not apply to one that is not certified.
instruments.what_it_does: The Commonwealth regulates the aircraft, the pilots and the airspace over this island completely. It does not regulate the island's airstrip as an aerodrome, because the strip is not certified. For an uncertified aircraft landing area the operator and the pilot in command decide whether it is fit to use.
instruments.quote_note: The category code published against Dunwich in the En Route Supplement Australia entry, which is the Commonwealth aeronautical publication. The same entry gives runway 15/33, unrated, grass, 800 m, slope 1.5 per cent, elevation 250 ft, CTAF 126.7, no fuel available, full NOTAM service not available, and this under additional information: animal hazard, kangaroo, exists on runway at all times.
instruments.why_it_matters: The island's third door, the one that turns a two hour medical transfer into twenty minutes, is a grass strip with kangaroos on it that no Commonwealth aerodrome standard binds. The airspace above it is regulated to the metre. That gap is the honest shape of Commonwealth authority in a small place.
instruments.gap: The ERSA page was read through a public mirror of the Commonwealth publication rather than from Airservices Australia directly, and the page carries the date 9 July 2026. Aerodrome data changes on a cycle. Read the current ERSA before relying on any figure here. The runway surface differs from the description in data/transport.json, which says gravel and topsoil from the airfield's own guidelines; both are recorded and neither is corrected here.

instruments.label: Commonwealth financial assistance grants to local government
instruments.the_part_that_bites: The Local Government (Financial Assistance) Act 1995, and the national principles made under it.
instruments.what_it_does: The Commonwealth pays untied grants to the states in two components, general purpose and local roads. The states pass them to councils on the recommendation of a state local government grants commission, in Queensland the Queensland Local Government Grants Commission. Once they reach a council the money is untied and the council decides what it is for.
instruments.why_it_matters: This is the honest answer to where federal money on this island comes from. It arrives as part of a council budget, allocated by a Queensland commission, and by the time it is spent on a road at Point Lookout nothing about it says Commonwealth. A player looking for a federal lever will not find one here, and that absence is itself the fact.
instruments.gap: No Redland City Council financial assistance grant figure is stated, and no island share of one. Council accounts were not read for this pack.

instruments.label: Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements 2018
instruments.the_part_that_bites: The arrangements themselves, activated per event, jointly funded by the Commonwealth and the state and in Queensland administered by the Queensland Reconstruction Authority.
instruments.what_it_does: Sets out the relief and recovery measures that can be funded after an eligible disaster and how the Commonwealth and the state share the cost. Replaced the Natural Disaster Relief and Recovery Arrangements on 1 November 2018.
instruments.why_it_matters: The most likely single moment the Commonwealth pays for something on this island is after a storm, and even then the money comes through a Queensland authority. A council that has just lost a foreshore does not ring Canberra.
instruments.gap: No cost-sharing percentage is stated here. The share varies by measure and by the state's expenditure against thresholds, and no figure was confirmed to this pack's standard.

instruments.label: Indigenous Rangers Program
instruments.what_it_does: A Commonwealth program administered by the National Indigenous Australians Agency that funds Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander land and sea management work. The agency publishes a Quandamooka Rangers project among the land and sea management projects it funds.
instruments.why_it_matters: The lever this pack calls ranger-program-funding has always named the Australian Government among its deciders and never named the program. This is it.
instruments.gap: The NIAA project page returned 403 to this agent and was identified through search results rather than read. No funding amount, no agreement term and no ranger headcount is stated here, and nothing is asserted about how QYAC runs the work. See docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md, which holds that QYAC has not seen this project.

instruments.label: Mobile Black Spot Program
instruments.what_it_does: Co-funds new and upgraded mobile base stations in regional and remote Australia, with the Commonwealth contributing up to 50 per cent of the total solution cost and the rest coming from carriers, state governments and councils. Rounds run periodically. Round 8 was announced as 55 million dollars of Commonwealth co-funding targeted at disaster-prone locations.
instruments.why_it_matters: The statutory infrastructure provider regime guarantees a connection to a house. Nothing guarantees a bar of signal on the road where somebody has just hit a koala, and this is the only Commonwealth mechanism that addresses that, on a competitive round, against every other regional place in Australia.
instruments.gap: Whether any Minjerribah site has ever been funded under any round was not established. Nothing here says the island has been in a round or has been passed over.

instruments.label: Biosecurity Act 2015
instruments.the_part_that_bites: Chapter 4, which manages the biosecurity risk of aircraft and vessels entering Australian territory from outside it, including by determining which landing places and ports are first points of entry.
instruments.what_it_does: Holds the national border against pests and diseases arriving from outside Australia.
instruments.why_it_matters: It is recorded here mostly for what it does not do. Nothing on Minjerribah is a first point of entry, so the biosecurity a player will actually meet on this island, the weeds, the fire ants, the foxes and the marine pests moving from the mainland, is Queensland's under the Biosecurity Act 2014, not the Commonwealth's. The Commonwealth's weight is at the border and in nationally cost-shared eradication programs such as the fire ant program, which every state, every territory and the Commonwealth fund and Queensland delivers.
instruments.gap: No fire ant detection on Minjerribah is claimed here and none was looked for. The point of this record is the division of responsibility, not the pest.

national_environmental_significance.about: The matters of national environmental significance this island actually carries, each named against the EPBC Act section that protects it and against the record in data/ecology.json the twin already simulates. This block is the join. It does not create a lever and it does not decide anything: it says what a proponent has to think about before doing something here, and what a player is looking at when the shorebird readout moves.
national_environmental_significance.handling: A matter listed here is a fact about Commonwealth law and about the ecology pack. It is not a claim that any particular lever needs a referral. Whether a specific action is likely to have a significant impact is a judgement for the proponent and then for the minister, and this project does not make it.

matters.here: The Moreton Bay Ramsar site, listed 22 October 1993, takes in North Stradbroke Island. Over 120,000 hectares bay-wide.

The eastern curlew and the bar-tailed godwit on the western sand flats, both on the annexes to the three bilateral migratory bird agreements. Moreton Bay is recorded as supporting some 28 species of migratory shorebirds and over 30,000 individuals in summer.
matters.note: The shorebird system already models a roost flush costing a bird fuel it has to make back before it can fly north. Nothing in the civic layer knew that was a Commonwealth matter.

matters.matter: Listed threatened species and ecological communities
matters.here: The eastern curlew is Critically Endangered and the bar-tailed godwit Endangered under the Act. The koala, in the combined Queensland, New South Wales and Australian Capital Territory populations, was listed as Endangered on 12 February 2022, which is the koala this island's habitat overlay argues about. The endangered swamp daisy Olearia hygrophila is published as found only on North Stradbroke Island.
matters.gap: The swamp daisy is not in data/ecology.json. It came out of a Queensland Wetlands Program fact sheet during this pass and has not been researched as a species record. Somebody should add it.

matters.epbc_section: section 23, with the whale offences at Part 13 Division 3
matters.here: The water beyond three nautical miles from the territorial sea baseline off the ocean coast, which is where the Australian Whale Sanctuary begins.

not_here.why: There is none on or around this island.

not_here.matter: The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park
not_here.why: It begins far to the north of Moreton Bay.

not_here.matter: Water resources from coal seam gas or a large coal mine
not_here.why: The island's mining was mineral sand and it ended in 2019. This trigger is specific to coal and coal seam gas and does not reach sand.
not_here.note: Worth stating plainly, because the island's aquifer is the thing most people would expect national water law to protect and it is not what that trigger is for.

commonwealth_money.about: How Commonwealth money reaches Minjerribah, and the honest shape of it, which is the thing a player should learn from this tier.
commonwealth_money.the_honest_note: Most federal money that lands on this island does not arrive from the Commonwealth. It arrives through Queensland, or through Redland City Council, having been paid to one of them first. By the time it is spent on a footpath or a ranger's wage, nothing about it is labelled federal. That is why a player who goes looking for a Commonwealth lever finds almost none, and it is not because the Commonwealth is not paying.

routes.reaches_the_island_via: The Queensland Reconstruction Authority, jointly funded with the state, activated per event
A National Indigenous Australians Agency program, direct to the funded organisation
routes.note: One of the few routes with no state or council in the middle of it.

routes.reaches_the_island_via: A competitive Commonwealth round, co-funded by carriers, the state and the council

commonwealth_money.gap: No dollar figure for any Commonwealth payment touching Minjerribah was established. This block describes routes, not amounts, and it should not be read as saying the Commonwealth spends much or little here.
