metrics.label: Annual visitors
metrics.note: About 375,000 in 2018, up from about 350,000 in 2017. Nobody has given this project a post-2019 figure.

metrics.label: Peak day load
metrics.note: How close a long weekend gets to the island's practical carrying limit. Modelling index.

metrics.label: Day visitor share
metrics.note: Estimate. Day trippers spend less per head and use the same road, carpark and toilet as an overnight guest.

metrics.label: Visitor satisfaction
metrics.note: Repeat visitation was reported at 79 per cent in the 2018 research round, which is the closest published proxy.

metrics.label: Resident amenity
metrics.note: Noise, traffic, parking, queueing, rubbish, and whether a local can get a park at their own beach.

metrics.label: Trust in the process
metrics.note: How far residents believe a decision was genuinely open. Starts low: the audit office found community oversight of the transition program was inadequate.

metrics.label: Peak barge queue
metrics.note: Vehicles waiting at Dunwich and Cleveland on a long weekend against sailing capacity. Capacity itself lives in data/transport.json.

metrics.label: Cost of the crossing
metrics.note: What it costs a household to use its only road. A flat vehicle fare of $59 standard and $69 large was in market to 31 March 2026, with a $20 surcharge on public holidays and the Christmas peak.

metrics.label: Ease of getting on and off
Parking pressure
metrics.note: Worst at Point Lookout around the gorge walk and Cylinder Beach in a peak week.

metrics.label: Camping capacity
metrics.note: Index rather than a count. Site totals belong in data/places.json and data/transport.json and were only partly verifiable: the camping operator's own site returned no route to this agent.

metrics.label: Camping and permit revenue
metrics.note: Goes to QYAC through Minjerribah Camping, so this metric is also a measure of Traditional Owner self-funding.

metrics.label: Long-term rental supply
metrics.note: Starts very low. Half the island's dwellings were unoccupied on census night and the island housing co-operative reported no vacancies across its portfolio.

metrics.label: Worker accommodation
metrics.note: Index. Council's housing plan records recruitment failing on the island for want of anywhere to live.

metrics.label: Short-stay letting stock
metrics.note: Index. Neither the council nor this pack has a verified count of short-stay listings on the island.

metrics.label: Permanent population
metrics.note: 2021 Census usual residents across the island, in 1,976 dwellings.

metrics.label: Business viability
metrics.note: Trade in June against overheads that do not go away in June.

metrics.label: Employment on Country
metrics.note: Ranger, camping, culture, land management and construction jobs held by Quandamooka people.

metrics.label: QYAC delivery capacity
metrics.note: The audit office found QYAC was handed several complex construction projects at once with fewer than 100 staff. Any lever that adds work to QYAC without adding capacity should push this down.

metrics.label: Cost of living
metrics.note: Everything on this island arrived on a barge.

metrics.label: Council budget headroom
metrics.note: Redland households were reported paying over $600 a year for waste alone, across nine contractors, eight waste centres and island barge logistics.

metrics.label: State appetite
metrics.note: Approved Minjerribah Futures funding rose from $20 million to $39.4 million, with $30.6 million spent as at April 2024. A further tranche is a political question, not a budget line.

metrics.label: Water security
metrics.note: The townships are off the South East Queensland Water Grid. Bulk water is drawn from bores and treated at small local plants.

metrics.label: Aquifer stress
metrics.note: The island's fresh water is the sand itself. The lakes and the wetlands sit on the same water the townships drink.

metrics.label: Wastewater headroom
metrics.note: The Point Lookout plant was rebuilt for $13.5 million and opened on 25 November 2016, rated at 1,600 kilolitres a day, more than twice the peak Christmas flow at the time, replacing a plant over 30 years old. Parts of all three townships still run on septic.

metrics.label: Amity Point erosion risk
metrics.note: Amity Point was the only area in the city assessed at high risk of coastal erosion in the 2016 current hazards work, and is a declared erosion prone area.

metrics.label: Property at risk
metrics.note: Public and private land has already been lost at Amity Point.

metrics.label: Koala population health
metrics.note: Island koalas carry the lowest genetic diversity of the south-east Queensland populations and are pressured by vehicle strike, dog attack and habitat loss. Council has run drone monitoring on the island.

metrics.label: Wildlife killed on roads
metrics.note: Wildlife Rescue Minjerribah reports more than 240 injured wildlife cases a year from vehicle strike or domestic pet attack combined.

metrics.label: Dog attacks on wildlife
metrics.note: Two koalas were killed and another badly injured by domestic dogs on the island in a cluster reported by the state environment department in 2024.

metrics.label: Fuel load near townships
metrics.note: QYAC leads the island's bushfire management, with Quandamooka Rangers conducting planned burns alongside QPWS.

metrics.label: Beach vehicle access
metrics.note: Good for the four-wheel-drive crowd is not good for the dune. Deliberately context rather than better or worse.

metrics.label: Emergency readiness
metrics.note: Heavily volunteer dependent. The volunteer base is ageing.

metrics.label: School enrolments
metrics.note: Downstream of whether working families can find a house.

metrics.label: Power reliability
metrics.note: The island is fed from the mainland grid rather than generated on. The pack does not claim the cable route, the feeder arrangement or an outage frequency, because none was verified.

levers.name: More barge sailings on a long weekend
levers.description: Add sailings across the Friday and the Monday of a long weekend so the queue at Toondah and at Dunwich clears instead of rolling over to the next boat.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for extra crewed sailings; no operator cost data was available

side_effects.description: More sailings means more cars, so the queue moves but the carparks at Point Lookout fill earlier.
Residents who wanted the crowd managed find the crowd increased instead.

levers.note: A private operator decides this on commercial grounds. A council or a player can ask. That is the whole point of the lever.

levers.name: Resident priority on peak barge bookings
levers.description: Hold a share of peak sailings for island residents and island-based trades so a local can still get home on the Sunday of a long weekend.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for booking system changes and verification

side_effects.description: Visitors turned away at Cleveland arrive angry or do not arrive at all, and the operators feel it in a shoulder week.
Proving who is a resident creates a small bureaucracy and a new grievance about who counts.

levers.note: No published resident quota exists on this route. This is a modelled option, not a current proposal.

levers.name: A resident fare for the crossing
levers.description: A standing concession on the vehicle and passenger fare for people who live here, on the argument that this crossing is their road rather than a day out.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate; the real number depends on whether the state subsidises the operator or regulates the fare

side_effects.description: Cheaper crossings mean more resident trips to the mainland, and some island trade moves to Cleveland.
Once a concession exists, every change to it becomes a fight.

levers.note: Islanders have been reported as excluded from the mainland 50 cent public transport fare, which is the live grievance this lever sits on. A petition for cheaper fares has been run publicly.

levers.name: Bring the crossing into the public transport network
levers.description: Treat the passenger crossing as a contracted public transport service with network fares and network obligations, the way the island bus routes already are.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a contracted service subsidy

side_effects.description: A cheap foot crossing pushes day visitor numbers up hard, and the island absorbs them without the vehicle constraint that used to hold them back.
Contracted service standards mean the timetable stops being the operator's to cut.

levers.note: Island bus services run under TransLink with 50 cent fares. The water crossing is the gap. Whether a ferry contract is legally or commercially available was not verified.

levers.name: Rebuild the mainland terminal
levers.description: Fix the island's front door: the terminal, the queueing, the parking and the pedestrian link at Toondah Harbour, without the residential development that carried it for a decade.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a terminal and queueing rebuild only, excluding any residential or marina component

side_effects.description: Five years of works at the only vehicle terminal makes the crossing worse before it gets better.
Any works in this location run into internationally protected wetland and migratory shorebird habitat.

levers.note: The private development partner withdrew its federal application in April 2024, days after the federal environment minister announced a proposed refusal. As reported in April 2026 the Priority Development Area remains in place with no private sector partner and no clear pathway. The withdrawn proposal had carried the new ferry terminal, which makes this the single largest open question in the access system.
levers.commonwealth_note: This is the only lever in the pack where the Commonwealth has already made a decision, and it is why the federal environment department is on the list of deciders. The minister's proposed refusal in April 2024 turned on the removal of 58.7 hectares from the Moreton Bay Ramsar site and on unacceptable impacts on threatened and migratory species including the eastern curlew. Four bodies across three governments now have to agree before the island's front door can be rebuilt, and the fourth of them has never had to come over.

levers.name: Dunwich gateway and foreshore works
levers.description: The island side: terminal arrival, foreshore, footpaths and the queueing area at Dunwich, as set up by the Gumpi master plan.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate; the master plan does not publish a costed works schedule

side_effects.description: Every gateway project on this island is also a cultural interpretation project, and that is QYAC's call to lead, which takes time the construction program does not allow for.
A nicer arrival raises day visitor volume without adding a single carpark at the other end of the island.

levers.name: More island buses, more of the year
levers.description: Lift service frequency between Dunwich, Amity Point and Point Lookout so arriving without a car is a real choice rather than a gamble.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for additional contracted services

side_effects.description: Buses only help if the boat and the bus meet. A timetable that misses the barge by ten minutes is worse than no bus.
Car-free day visitors spend less per head but leave less mess and take no parking space.

levers.note: Real and recent, from 1 December 2025: 41 new weekly services on route 880 between Dunwich and Point Lookout with an earlier first departure and a later last return, a further 91 weekly services in peak holiday seasons, route 881 extended from One Mile through Dunwich to Amity Point with 112 weekly services, and a new stop at the Quandamooka arts and culture centre. Fifty cent fares apply.

levers.name: Cap day visitor vehicles in peak periods
levers.description: Limit how many non-resident vehicles can land on a peak day, so the island's roads and carparks are sized to the island rather than to demand.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for administration and enforcement

side_effects.description: The cap redistributes rather than removes: the days either side of the cap fill up instead.
A public island that turns people away becomes a political story on the mainland, where most of the voters are.

levers.note: Nobody has proposed this. It is here because it is the lever residents describe wanting when they describe a long weekend, and because its trade-offs are honest.

levers.name: A proper holding area for the barge queue
levers.description: Get the departing vehicle queue off the Dunwich streets and into a marshalled area with shade, toilets and a live boarding call.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for land, pavement, shade and amenities

side_effects.description: A comfortable queue is a longer tolerated queue, so the operator has less pressure to add sailings.
Land at Dunwich is scarce and contested; using it for cars is a choice against using it for housing.

levers.name: Park and ride on the mainland side
levers.description: Make it easy to leave the car at Cleveland: secure parking, a shuttle, and a fare that makes walking on cheaper than driving on.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate

side_effects.description: Only works if the island bus meets the boat. Without that it is a carpark nobody uses.
Cleveland residents get the carpark and the traffic, and they are in the same council division as the island.

levers.name: Cap camping sites across the island
levers.description: Hold total camping sites at or below today's number instead of adding sites into the peak, and take the pressure through pricing and season instead.

cost_aud.basis: a cap costs nothing to declare and costs forgone revenue to hold

side_effects.description: Sites that sell out earlier push the overflow into illegal camping on road reserves and tracks.
Camping revenue is QYAC revenue, so a cap is also a cut to Traditional Owner self-funding.

levers.name: Set beach camping numbers on Main and Flinders
levers.description: How many parties can camp on the open beach at once. The beach camping areas sit inside the Minjerribah Recreation Area, so this is a joint management decision.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for ranger patrol time at a higher compliance level

side_effects.description: Fewer beach sites means more pressure on the township grounds, which are next door to houses.
Tighter numbers only bind if somebody drives the beach and checks, which is ranger time nobody has funded.

levers.name: Enforce against illegal camping
levers.description: Patrol the road reserves, carparks and tracks where people sleep in vans without a booking, and actually issue the notices.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for two additional compliance officers through the peak season

side_effects.description: Some of the vans are workers with a job on the island and nowhere to live, so enforcement lands on the housing problem rather than on tourism.
Enforcement without an alternative shifts the same vans to the next street.

levers.note: That some illegal campers are island workers is an inference from the housing evidence, not a counted fact.

levers.name: Price the shoulder season down and the peak up
levers.description: Use camping and permit pricing to move visitors out of six brutal weekends and into the forty other weeks, when the businesses need them and the island can carry them.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for systems and marketing

side_effects.description: A busier winter means the island never gets its quiet months back, which is the thing long-term residents most quietly value.
Year-round trade makes year-round jobs, which makes the housing shortage bite harder.

levers.name: Set the vehicle access permit price
levers.description: What it costs to drive on Main Beach and Flinders Beach. The permit is the only real lever on how many vehicles are on the sand at once.

cost_aud.basis: a price change is revenue, not cost

side_effects.description: Price rises land hardest on island families who drive the beach as ordinary transport, not as recreation.
A dearer permit makes driving without one more attractive, and enforcement is a long beach.

levers.note: Permits are sold by Minjerribah Camping online and in person. Current prices were not readable by this agent: the operator's site refused the connection. Do not put a dollar figure in the game until somebody checks it.

levers.name: Close sections of beach in the shorebird season
levers.description: Keep vehicles off the sections where migratory shorebirds roost, in the months they are here, with signage and ranger presence rather than a gate.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for signage, fencing and patrols

side_effects.description: Traffic concentrates onto the sections still open, so the damage moves rather than falls.
Closures announced without local input are the fastest way to lose the fishing and four-wheel-drive crowd on every other question.

levers.note: The species and roost locations belong in data/ecology.json. This pack does not name a beach section, because none was verified.

levers.name: Manage parking at Point Lookout
levers.description: Time limits, resident permits, or paid parking around the gorge walk and Cylinder Beach, where the carparks are full by mid-morning through the season.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for signage, machines or permit administration and enforcement

side_effects.description: Displaced cars park on residential streets and verges, and the complaint moves one block inland.
Paid parking at a public beach on a public island is the kind of decision that defines a council term.

levers.note: This is one of the few levers on this list a council genuinely controls on its own, which is exactly why it attracts the heat.

levers.name: Manage the crowd on the gorge walk
levers.description: One-way flow, timed entry at peak, better dispersal onto the coastal walk, and interpretation that QYAC leads rather than a council sign writer.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for path works, wayfinding and interpretation

side_effects.description: Dispersing the crowd onto the coastal link spreads the wear onto headland vegetation that was never carrying it.
Interpretation done properly needs QYAC time, and QYAC time is the scarcest resource in this whole file.

levers.note: The Minjerribah Panorama Coastal Walk is a real council project delivered with QYAC, linking Point Lookout village to Cylinder Beach. The timed-entry and one-way elements described here are modelled options on top of it, not part of that project.

levers.name: A visitor levy on paid accommodation
levers.description: A per-night charge on paid stays, hypothecated to the things visitors wear out: toilets, carparks, tracks, rubbish and ranger time.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for collection and administration

side_effects.description: A levy on paid beds is invisible to the day visitor who drives on, uses the toilet block and drives off, which is most of the load.
Hypothecated money has a way of becoming general revenue by the third budget.

levers.note: A local government in Queensland cannot simply impose a bed tax. This needs the state, which is why player_role is advocate.

levers.name: Register every short-stay letting
levers.description: Make every whole-house holiday letting register with the council, with a contact who answers the phone at midnight and a fee that funds compliance.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a register, one compliance officer and a complaints line

side_effects.description: A register is the precondition for every other housing lever, because right now nobody knows how many there are.
Owners who let a few weeks a year to cover rates find the paperwork not worth it, and some of those houses simply sit empty instead of returning to long-term rental.

levers.note: Council publishes guidance on short-term accommodation and Airbnb; whether a registration scheme exists on the island was not confirmed. Brisbane consulted on a short stay accommodation local law in 2025, which is the nearest live precedent.

levers.name: Cap short-stay lettings by township
levers.description: Set a ceiling on the share of dwellings in each township that can be let short-stay, with Point Lookout hitting the ceiling first.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for administration, appeals and legal exposure

side_effects.description: Capped supply raises the nightly rate on the beds that remain, so visitor spend per head rises while visitor numbers fall.
Owners appeal, and a small council spends years defending a scheme amendment.

levers.note: Half the island's private dwellings were unoccupied on census night and 65 per cent at Point Lookout. That is the number this lever is aimed at. Whether a cap would actually convert those houses to rentals is genuinely unknown.

levers.name: Build worker accommodation
levers.description: Purpose-built beds for the chefs, nurses, rangers, deckhands and cleaners the island cannot recruit because there is nowhere for them to live.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for roughly 40 beds including island construction premium and barge freight

side_effects.description: Employer-tied housing means losing the job means losing the bed, which is its own kind of insecurity.
Every tonne of material comes over on the barge, so the build costs more and takes longer than the mainland comparison the budget was written against.

levers.name: Expand community housing
levers.description: Add to the island's community housing portfolio, which has run at no vacancy across the whole portfolio.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for around 30 dwellings at island construction cost

side_effects.description: Land suitable for housing at Dunwich is also the land wanted for the gateway, the depot and the queue.
New dwellings need water and sewer connections in townships where parts still run on septic.

levers.note: Council's housing plan records the island housing co-operative holding a portfolio of about 44 properties with no vacancies. The figure was read through a search extract, not from the plan itself.

levers.name: Release the master-planned land at Dunwich
levers.description: Give effect to the Gumpi master plan land uses so residential, commercial and community land can actually be built on rather than studied.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for enabling infrastructure, not the buildings

side_effects.description: Growth at Dunwich is growth against koala habitat and against the aquifer that supplies the town.
Land dealings on Country need QYAC agreement, and that is a process with its own timeline.

levers.name: A rates differential on long-empty dwellings
levers.description: Charge a higher general rate on dwellings that sit empty most of the year, on the argument that an empty house uses the road, the water main and the tip anyway.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for assessment and objections handling

side_effects.description: The obvious way to avoid the differential is to let the house short-stay, which is the opposite of what the lever wanted.
Holiday home owners are ratepayers with time, money and lawyers, and they vote in the same division.

levers.note: Whether Queensland local government rating powers support a differential framed this way was not verified. Treat as a design idea, not advice.

levers.name: Fast-track granny flats for long-term letting
levers.description: Make a secondary dwelling easy and cheap to approve on an island block, on the condition it is let long-term rather than by the night.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for assessment resourcing and a fee waiver pool

side_effects.description: More dwellings on the same block on septic is a wastewater problem before it is a housing solution.
The long-term letting condition is only worth what the enforcement behind it is worth.

levers.name: Build the buried seawall at Amity Point
levers.description: The southern reach recommendation from the shoreline plan: a buried seawall with sand over it, so the beach looks like a beach until the day it has to hold.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate; council has budgeted for design and approvals but no published construction figure was found

side_effects.description: A wall holds the land and loses the beach in front of it over time, which is the trade nobody wants to say out loud at the meeting.
Rock may come from council's own island quarry, which is cheaper but ties the project to a supply council cannot guarantee the price of.

levers.note: Council has allocated funding towards design and approvals for a buried seawall on the foreshore near the campground. The construction cost above is this pack's estimate, not council's.

levers.name: Nourish the beach at Amity Point
levers.description: Put sand back, repeatedly. Cheap to start, never finished, and the only option that keeps a beach in front of the houses.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for an initial placement and repeat campaigns

side_effects.description: The sand leaves. This is a recurring cost forever, and the first time a budget skips a campaign the gains are gone.
Placement works disturb the nearshore and the seagrass edge while they run.

levers.name: Formalise and maintain the flow slide barrier
levers.description: The central reach recommendation: turn the ad hoc rock along the foreshore into a maintained structure, with the cost split between council assets and private land behind it.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate; the split between council and private landowners is set by whose asset is protected

side_effects.description: Landowners who cannot fund their section leave a gap, and the sea finds the gap.
A hard edge in the central reach steepens the problem at the ends of it.

levers.note: Council is responsible for its own land and assets and for the sections of barrier that protect local roads and parks. Private landowners bear construction and maintenance for works protecting their properties. That split is the drama.

levers.name: Managed retreat at Amity Point
levers.description: Buy back and remove the most exposed properties over time instead of defending them, and let the shoreline move.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for voluntary acquisition of a small number of foreshore properties at island values

side_effects.description: Announcing retreat as an option collapses property values before a single house is bought, which is why councils do not say the word.
Amity Point has no progress association left to negotiate through, so the conversation happens house by house.

levers.note: Retreat is a standard option in coastal adaptation strategy and is not a current Amity Point proposal. Modelled here because a civic game that only offers armouring is lying about the choice. The Amity Point Progress Association wound up in 2024, per docs/DATA-NOTES.md.

levers.name: Fund the coastal process research
levers.description: Keep surveying the northern reach and keep funding the university work on why the flow slides happen, so the next decision is made on evidence rather than on the last big storm.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for surveys and a research partnership

side_effects.description: Research is also the respectable way to defer a decision for another four years, and residents know it.

levers.note: Council is funding research with the University of Queensland into the flow slide mechanism, and the northern reach recommendation is surveys and coastal process studies.

levers.name: Dune restoration and formed beach accesses
levers.description: Fence, plant and formalise the walking accesses so people stop cutting new tracks over the foredune at every beach entrance.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for accesses, fencing, plants and volunteer support

side_effects.description: Formed accesses concentrate foot traffic, which is better for the dune and worse for the two spots where everybody now walks.
The planting only survives if volunteers keep watering it through the first summer, and the volunteer base is ageing.

levers.name: Storm tide and evacuation readiness
levers.description: Plan for the day the barge cannot run and the island has to look after itself: shelter, supplies, comms and a rehearsed plan for each township.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for shelter upgrades, generators, comms and exercises

side_effects.description: Readiness that depends on volunteers ages with the volunteers.
A hardened hall is also the hall the community loses for three months while it is upgraded.

levers.note: Redland City Council maintains a public disaster plan covering its islands. This pack does not restate its content because it was not read in full.
levers.commonwealth_note: Recovery after an eligible disaster runs through the Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements, which the Commonwealth and Queensland fund jointly and the Queensland Reconstruction Authority administers. That is why the Commonwealth is a decider on this lever and on almost nothing else in the hazard part of this pack: it does not decide the readiness, it decides half of the money afterwards.

levers.name: Upgrade the transfer station and extend its hours
levers.description: Longer opening, better sorting bays and a proper hardstand at the island recycling and waste centre, so a load gets separated instead of all going in the one bin.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for civil works and additional staffed hours

side_effects.description: Longer hours are longer wages, and the saving on export tonnage takes years to catch up with them.
Easier tipping means more tipping, including mainland loads brought over by trades.

levers.note: Non-commercial residential use by island residents is free. Commercial users and non-residents pay. Opening hours were not verified and are not stated here.

levers.name: Change how often waste leaves the island
levers.description: Every skip of rubbish goes on a barge. More runs means less smell and fewer overflowing bays; fewer runs means a smaller bill and a fuller yard.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for additional contracted barge movements

side_effects.description: Redland's waste system already runs nine contractors, eight waste centres and island barge logistics, and every household pays for it whether they use it or not.
More heavy vehicle movements through Dunwich on the way to the ramp.

levers.name: A reuse shop and repair space at the tip
levers.description: Take the good stuff off the pile before it gets on the barge, and sell it back on the island.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a shed, hardstand and two positions

side_effects.description: A tip shop on an island where everything costs a barge trip becomes a genuine social hub, which is worth more than the tonnage.
It competes, quietly, with the island's own retailers.

levers.name: Mulch green waste on the island
levers.description: Chip and compost garden waste here instead of barging it to the mainland, and give the mulch back for dune work, parks and gardens.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a chipper, pad and operator

side_effects.description: A green waste pile in a fire-prone landscape is a fuel load with a fence around it.
Free mulch encourages more clearing, some of it in habitat.

levers.name: Change what commercial loads pay at the tip
levers.description: The fee a builder or a business pays to tip on the island, against the cost of getting that same load onto a barge.

cost_aud.basis: revenue lever, not a spending one

side_effects.description: Every dollar on a commercial load is a dollar of temptation to dump it in the bush instead.
Trades pass it straight through to island customers, who already pay a barge premium on everything.

levers.name: Extend the sewer to properties still on septic
levers.description: Connect more of Dunwich, Amity Point and Point Lookout to the sewer instead of leaving them on septic systems over a shallow water table beside the bay.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate scaled from council's earlier $5 million three-year Point Lookout extension program

side_effects.description: Connection charges land on households who did not ask for the works and were managing fine.
Sewer is the quiet precondition for density, so this lever unlocks housing levers that were previously impossible.

levers.note: Parts of all three townships not served by the network use septic systems. Council previously ran a $5 million three-year program to extend the Point Lookout network, and a project to lift Dunwich connections above 75 per cent of properties from a base of 128 connected.

levers.name: Use treated wastewater instead of drinking water
levers.description: Put treated effluent from the Point Lookout plant onto ovals, gardens and dust suppression, so the bores are not being drawn down to water a football field.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for storage, pipework and a small reticulation network

side_effects.description: Recycled water schemes need somewhere to put the water in a wet winter, and that is a storage nobody budgeted for.
Public acceptance of recycled water is its own campaign, and a badly run one poisons the next twenty years.

levers.note: The Point Lookout plant was rebuilt for $13.5 million and opened in November 2016 with capacity for future peak demand. Whether it currently produces recycled water was not verified.

levers.name: Monitor the borefield and the lakes properly
levers.description: Instrument the aquifer, publish the numbers, and set trigger levels, so a dry year is seen coming rather than announced.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for bores, telemetry and analysis

side_effects.description: Publishing the numbers means publishing the bad years too, and the first bad year becomes a story about the lakes.
Good data makes the case for the water reserves being real allocations rather than paper ones.

levers.note: Two water reserves totalling 61,190 megalitres were established for the Quandamooka People in December 2023 from water previously allocated to sand mining, split evenly between environmental and cultural use and economic use and rehabilitation.

levers.name: Peak period water restrictions
levers.description: Restrict outdoor water use through the weeks when the island's population triples and the bores work hardest.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for communications and compliance

side_effects.description: Restrictions that bind on residents and not on visitor accommodation are read as exactly what they are.
Gardens and street trees die in the summer they are needed most for shade.

levers.name: Renew the main island road
levers.description: Resurfacing, shoulders and drainage on the road between the townships, which carries every barge load, every bus and every tourist that lands.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a renewal program plus ongoing maintenance

side_effects.description: A better road is a faster road, and faster roads on this island kill more wildlife.
Roadworks on the only route between townships means detours nobody has an alternative to.

levers.note: Road names and alignments are in data/geography.json. This lever deliberately names no road segment that has not been verified there.

levers.name: Lower speeds and build wildlife crossings
levers.description: Night speed limits, signage that means something, and fauna crossings where the koalas and kangaroos actually cross.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for signage, treatments and a small number of crossing structures

side_effects.description: A slower island road adds minutes to a barge run, and people who are late for a boat do not slow down.
Crossings only work where the animals already move, and the mapping to prove that costs more than the sign.

levers.note: Wildlife Rescue Minjerribah reports more than 240 injured wildlife cases a year from vehicle strike or domestic pet attack combined. The split between the two causes was not published.

levers.name: Footpaths and a safe bike route
levers.description: Connect the townships and the beaches on foot and by bike so a kid, a pram or a walking frame is not on the road shoulder.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a staged path network

side_effects.description: Paths through vegetation are clearing, however narrow, and this island's vegetation is habitat.
A good path becomes the tourist route, and the quiet street stops being quiet.

levers.name: Maintain the beach access tracks
levers.description: Grade and stabilise the sand tracks onto the beaches, because a chewed-out track is how a dune gets cut in half.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for plant time and matting

side_effects.description: Easier tracks bring more vehicles, and the improvement is spent within two seasons.
Every hour of ranger plant time on tracks is an hour not spent on weeds, fire or compliance.

levers.name: Island energy resilience
levers.description: Solar and storage at the places that must keep running when the mainland supply drops: the water plants, the sewage plant, the halls used as shelters, the clinic.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for behind-the-meter solar and battery at critical sites

side_effects.description: Batteries in a fire landscape need their own separation and their own fire plan.
Critical-site resilience does nothing for a household whose power is off, which is who complains.

levers.note: The island's supply arrangement from the mainland grid was not verified in detail, so this lever describes site resilience rather than a network change.

levers.name: Protect koala habitat in the planning scheme
levers.description: Map the habitat and put a real overlay over it, so clearing for a new house is assessed rather than assumed.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for mapping, scheme amendment and assessment resourcing

side_effects.description: Every housing lever in this file gets harder the day this one passes. That tension is the game.
An overlay without enforcement is a map, and clearing happens on weekends.

levers.note: Council has run drone koala monitoring on the island. Island koalas carry the lowest genetic diversity of the south-east Queensland populations, which makes habitat loss here harder to recover from than on the mainland.

levers.name: Enforce dog control
levers.description: Registration checks, containment orders, trapping of roaming dogs, and penalties that actually issue.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for island-based inspector time and equipment

side_effects.description: Enforcement against neighbours in a town of a few hundred people is personal in a way it never is in a city.
Fewer roaming dogs also means fewer dogs chasing roos into traffic, which shows up in the road numbers before it shows up in the koala numbers.

levers.note: Two koalas were killed and another badly injured by domestic dogs in a cluster reported by the state environment department in 2024. Council has run trapping programs alongside state agencies, and has authorised staff at island organisations to help its dog inspectors.

levers.name: Review the off-lead areas
levers.description: Where a dog can legally be off a lead, and where it cannot, on beaches shared with roosting birds and a koala population.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for signage and consultation

side_effects.description: Dog owners are a constituency that turns up to every meeting for a decade about this one thing.
Restricting the popular beach concentrates dogs onto the remaining one.

levers.note: Existing off-lead area locations were not verified and are not named here.

levers.name: Fund the wildlife rescue volunteers
levers.description: Vehicles, fuel, cages, vet costs and training for the volunteers who pick up every hit koala and every dog-mauled roo on this island.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a small volunteer service

side_effects.description: Funding the rescue can become the reason not to fix the cause, and the volunteers are the first to say so.

levers.name: How much of the island gets burnt
levers.description: The size of the annual planned burn program: hazard reduction around the townships and the fire-prone edges, run by the Quandamooka Rangers with QPWS.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for crews, plant and contractors across a season

side_effects.description: The complaints arrive in the week of the burn; the benefit arrives in a summer that then does not happen, so nobody credits it.
Burning is skilled work with a narrow weather window, and doing more of it needs people and gear that are not on the island in June.

levers.note: QYAC leads the island's bushfire management, and the Quandamooka Rangers conduct planned burns and wildfire response with QPWS. This lever models the scale of that program. It does not depict, name or animate cultural burning practice, which is a QYAC decision and is queued in docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md.

levers.name: Notify and time the burns around the community
levers.description: Tell people before the smoke arrives, avoid the school run and the long weekend, and give anyone with a lung condition a day's warning.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for notification systems and coordination

side_effects.description: Narrowing the acceptable days narrows an already narrow weather window, and some burns simply do not happen.

levers.note: Seqwater publishes planned burn notices for its island landholding, including expected smoke direction. Multiple agencies burn on this island, which is exactly why coordination is a lever.

levers.name: Feral animal and weed control
levers.description: Foxes, feral cats, roaming dogs and the weed fronts. Slow, unglamorous, and the difference between a national park and a paddock.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a sustained control program

side_effects.description: Baiting and trapping near townships needs domestic pets contained first, which sends this straight back into the dog fight.
Stop for one budget cycle and the fronts come back further ahead than where they started.

levers.note: Joint management rangers lead fire, pests and weeds, cultural heritage and asset work on park. Species detail belongs in data/ecology.json.

levers.name: The pace of mine rehabilitation and handback
levers.description: How fast the former mining land is rehabilitated, surrendered and added to the park or returned to Traditional Owners.

cost_aud.basis: borne by the former operator under its rehabilitation obligations, not by council or the player

side_effects.description: Rehabilitation work is the closest thing the island has to a post-mining trades pipeline, and it ends.
Land added to the park is land that cannot be built on, which the housing levers then have to work around.

levers.note: Sibelco signed a rehabilitation agreement in December 2019 committing to work with QYAC on rehabilitating and surrendering former mining land. Reported figures at the time included a commitment covering over 12,000 hectares and more than 2,200 hectares of lease already surrendered. Current progress was not verified for this pack.

levers.name: Fund the ranger program properly
levers.description: More Quandamooka rangers, funded for longer than a grant cycle, doing the fire, weeds, compliance, cultural heritage and visitor work the island already relies on.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for an expanded ranger team with vehicles and plant

side_effects.description: Rangers need somewhere to live, and the island does not have it, so the jobs go to people who commute or do not go at all.
A well-resourced ranger service becomes the agency everyone calls for everything, including things it was never funded for.

levers.commonwealth_note: The Australian Government has always been on this lever's list of deciders and the program behind it was never named. It is the Indigenous Rangers Program, run by the National Indigenous Australians Agency, and the agency publishes a Quandamooka Rangers project among the land and sea management work it funds. This is one of the few routes by which Commonwealth money reaches this island without passing through Queensland or the council first. Nothing here says what the agreement contains or how QYAC runs the work.

levers.name: Invest in Traditional Owner led tourism
levers.description: Back the cultural and eco-tourism the transition was always supposed to build, on QYAC's terms and at QYAC's pace.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate; individual project budgets under Minjerribah Futures were not itemised for this pack

side_effects.description: Handing several complex construction projects to one organisation at once is exactly what the audit office found went wrong last time.
Successful cultural tourism raises visitor numbers, which lands straight back on the barge queue and the carparks.

levers.note: The audit office found the transition strategy assumed $36.6 million of private investment that never arrived, and that QYAC was assigned several complex construction projects at once with fewer than 100 staff and no adequate capacity assessment. Any version of this lever that ignores capacity repeats the finding.

levers.name: Buy local and train local
levers.description: Write island employment and island suppliers into every contract council and the state let on this island, and fund the training that makes it possible.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for procurement administration and training subsidy

side_effects.description: Local content requirements raise the tendered price, and the difference comes out of the same capital budget that was buying the thing.
The island has a small pool of qualified trades, so a big program simply bids against itself.

levers.name: Do something about the cost of a barge trip on everything
levers.description: Freight relief, a consolidated island delivery run, or a community bulk buy: anything that stops every carton of milk carrying a boat fare.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a freight subsidy or a consolidated run

side_effects.description: A subsidy on freight is a subsidy to whoever controls the freight, unless the pass-through is policed.
Cheaper freight makes it cheaper to bring everything from the mainland, including the things the island could make or grow.

levers.name: Ask the state for the next transition tranche
levers.description: Go back for another round of transition funding, with the audit findings on the table and a governance model that answers them.

cost_aud.basis: the ask itself costs nothing; the delivery is priced in the levers it funds

side_effects.description: The last program was found to have complex, inconsistent governance and inadequate community oversight, so the next one arrives with conditions attached.
A state that believes the transition is finished reads the ask as a failure to acquit the last one.

levers.name: Change how the island is consulted
levers.description: A standing island reference group that meets on the island, sees drafts before they are decided, and gets an answer in writing.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for secretariat, sitting fees and travel

side_effects.description: Every lever in this file gets slower once there is a group that must be consulted on it.
A reference group that is overruled twice is worse than no reference group at all.
Amity Point has no progress association left, so getting a representative voice from that township takes deliberate effort.

levers.note: The audit office found governance arrangements complex and inconsistent, lacking adequate community oversight. This lever is the direct answer to that finding.

levers.name: Extend health services on the island
levers.description: More clinic hours, better after-hours cover and telehealth that works, on an island with a median age of 52 and a boat between it and a hospital.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for extended clinic staffing and equipment

side_effects.description: Clinical staff need housing, and the housing is the bottleneck, not the funding.
Better island health services reduce the trips to the mainland that keep the ferry timetable justified.

levers.note: Service providers on the island are listed in data/businesses.json. Staffing levels, rosters and after-hours arrangements were not verified and are not stated.
levers.commonwealth_note: The Australian Government is on this lever because primary care is largely a Commonwealth responsibility and the state runs the hospital on the other side of the water. Neither government has an office here. This pack does not state what either currently funds on the island.

levers.name: Put the island's black spots into a Commonwealth round
levers.description: Nominate the roads and beaches with no mobile signal for a co-funded base station, and put up the council's share, against every other regional place in Australia asking for the same thing.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate of a council co-contribution to one co-funded site. The Commonwealth contributes up to 50 per cent of total solution cost and no site cost for this island has been published.

side_effects.description: A tower has to stand somewhere, and on this island the somewhere with the coverage is the ridge with the view.
Coverage where there was none brings people to places that were quiet because nobody could be reached there.

levers.status_note: modelled_option means this pack built the framing. The program is real and cited; no nomination of any Minjerribah site is claimed, and whether the island has ever been in a round was not established.
levers.commonwealth_note: This is the clearest Commonwealth-first lever in the pack, and it is a good lesson in what that tier is like from here. Nobody on this island decides it. The council can co-fund and the state can co-fund, and then it goes into a national competitive round. The statutory infrastructure provider regime already guarantees a house a connection; nothing guarantees a bar of signal on the road where somebody has just hit a koala. That gap is what this lever is about.

levers.name: Monitor the western flats against the wetland's listed character
levers.description: Count the birds, map the roosts and record the disturbance on the bay-side flats on a schedule, so a change in the internationally listed wetland is something somebody noticed rather than something somebody later inferred.

cost_aud.basis: modelling estimate for a seasonal count and roost survey program with local volunteers, equipment and a coordinator

side_effects.description: A monitoring program that finds decline gives every future proposal a harder number to argue with, including the ones the island wants.
Counting is not protecting. A funded survey can become the answer given whenever anybody asks what is being done.

levers.status_note: modelled_option means this pack built the framing. The listing, the obligation to maintain ecological character and the species are cited; no current monitoring proposal for this island is claimed and none was found.
levers.commonwealth_note: Australia's obligation as a party to the Ramsar Convention is to maintain the ecological character of a listed site and to report change in it. The site is Moreton Bay and it takes in this island. The twin already models a roost flush costing a bird the fuel it needs to reach the northern hemisphere, in src/systems/ecology/shorebirds.js, and until now the civic layer had no idea that was a national matter.

issues.label: The barge queue on a long weekend
issues.one_line: One vehicle route, a private operator, and a Sunday afternoon when the whole island wants to leave at once.
issues.primary_tension: More sailings solve the queue and worsen everything the queue was accidentally protecting.

issues.label: What it costs to get home
issues.one_line: The island's only road has a fare on it, and the mainland's cheap public transport fare does not apply.
issues.primary_tension: Somebody has to pay: the operator, the state, or the household.

issues.label: The island's front door
issues.one_line: The mainland terminal has no development partner and no settled plan, and the island end is still a master plan.
issues.primary_tension: Fixing access invites more of what access already delivers.

issues.label: Getting around without a car
issues.one_line: Twenty-odd kilometres between the boat and the surf, and a bus that has to meet both.
issues.primary_tension: Buses only work if the timetable respects the boat.

issues.label: Visitor numbers versus resident amenity
issues.one_line: Around 375,000 visitors a year against about 2,150 residents, most of it landing in six weekends.
issues.primary_tension: Every business needs the peak and every resident dreads it.

issues.label: Camping capacity and illegal camping
issues.one_line: Bookings that sell out months ahead, and vans sleeping on road reserves in between.
issues.primary_tension: Capping sites protects the dunes and pushes people into the bush.

issues.label: Four-wheel-drive beach access
issues.one_line: A vehicle access permit, two beaches, tide windows, and a dune underneath all of it.
issues.primary_tension: The beach is a road for some people and a habitat for others, and both are right.

issues.label: Who pays for the visitors
issues.one_line: Toilets, carparks, tracks and rubbish are paid for by residents and used by everybody.
issues.primary_tension: The people who cost the most are the hardest to charge.

issues.label: Short-stay letting, rentals and worker housing
issues.one_line: Half the dwellings empty on census night, no vacancies in community housing, and businesses that cannot recruit.
issues.primary_tension: Every dwelling is somebody's investment and somebody else's home.

issues.label: Amity Point erosion
issues.one_line: The only part of the city assessed at high risk of coastal erosion, with land already lost and a 20 year plan split into three reaches.
issues.primary_tension: Armour, nourish or retreat, and each one takes something from somebody.

issues.label: Dunes and beach access
issues.one_line: Every informal track over a foredune is a future blowout.
issues.primary_tension: Making access easy makes damage easy.

issues.label: Storm tide and being cut off
issues.one_line: The day the barge cannot run, the island is on its own.
issues.primary_tension: Readiness is expensive and invisible until it is not.

issues.label: Getting the rubbish off the island
issues.one_line: Every skip goes on a barge, and Redland households already pay over $600 a year for waste.
issues.primary_tension: Cheaper waste means more waste sitting on the island for longer.

issues.label: Sewage and the sea
issues.one_line: A rebuilt plant at Point Lookout, septic systems across all three townships, and a bay on the other side of the dune.
issues.primary_tension: Connecting people to sewer is expensive, unpopular, and the precondition for everything else.

issues.label: Water security
issues.one_line: The townships are off the water grid and drink what the sand holds.
issues.primary_tension: The same water supplies the town, the lakes and the wetlands.

issues.label: Roads, paths and maintenance
issues.one_line: One main road between three townships, carrying everything that lands.
issues.primary_tension: A better road is a faster road.

issues.label: Dogs, cars and wildlife
issues.one_line: More than 240 injured wildlife cases a year on this island from vehicle strike and domestic pet attack, and a koala population with the lowest genetic diversity in the region.
issues.primary_tension: Enforcement in a small town is personal.

issues.label: Hazard reduction versus smoke
issues.one_line: QYAC leads the island's fire management, and the smoke arrives over the same townships the burn is protecting.
issues.primary_tension: The complaint is immediate and the benefit is a fire that never happens.

issues.label: Power and critical services
issues.one_line: Supply comes from the mainland, and the water plants, the sewage plant and the shelters all run on it.
issues.primary_tension: Resilience at critical sites does nothing for a household with no power.

issues.label: Life after the mine
issues.one_line: Mining ended in 2019 under a 2011 statute, and the transition program has been audited once already.
issues.primary_tension: The transition asked one organisation to build a new economy while also being the native title holder, the joint manager and the camping operator.

issues.label: The cost of living on an island
issues.one_line: Everything arrived on a barge and the price says so.
issues.primary_tension: Cheaper freight makes it cheaper to import what the island could make.

issues.label: Who actually decides
issues.one_line: One councillor shared with a mainland suburb, two state departments, a native title body corporate, a joint management arrangement and three private operators.
issues.primary_tension: Almost nothing on this island is decided by the people who live on it.

issues.label: Health and services
issues.one_line: Median age 52, and a boat between the island and a hospital.
issues.primary_tension: Funding a service is easy; housing the person who delivers it is not.

sim_defaults.mood_note: Group mood drifts back toward base_mood at this rate. A win fades. A grievance fades slower: use half this rate for negative movements.
sim_defaults.effect_ramp: Apply an effect as a linear ramp from delay_months to delay_months plus half the lead time, not as a step. Nothing on this island happens on the day it is announced.
sim_defaults.consultation_trust_rule: Any lever with player_role of player_decides that is enacted without the consultation-model lever active should apply an extra -0.05 to consultation_trust. Being right is not the same as being consulted.
sim_defaults.qyac_capacity_rule: If more than two levers whose who_decides includes qyac are in delivery at once, halve the magnitude of all their effects and double their lead_time_months. This is the audit office finding, expressed as a rule.
sim_defaults.seasonality: Peak load runs the Queensland school holidays, Easter and every long weekend. Winter is whale season and a quieter kind of busy. The island at census time in August is the island at its emptiest.
sim_defaults.clock: world.clock. No lever in this file may be evaluated against wall time.

gaps: No lever cost in this file was quoted by the body that would pay it, except where a published figure is cited in the note.

The Redland Local Housing Action Plan PDF, the Amity Point SEMP northern reach page and the council operational plan performance reports all returned 403 to this agent. Their figures reached this pack through search extracts only.
The two Quandamooka ILUAs were not read. Their schedules govern camping, tourism and land dealings, and several levers here assume a decision path that those documents may set differently.
No current visitor number after 2018 was found. Everything downstream of visitor_volume inherits that gap.
Whether the Gumpi master plan has been given effect in the current Redland City Plan was not confirmed.

No EPBC Act referral for anything on Minjerribah itself was found or read. The only Commonwealth environmental decision this pack records is the Toondah one on the mainland side of the crossing, and every other statement about where the Act would bite is the Act's own text applied to what the ecology pack already records, not a case.

The cadastral boundary of the Moreton Bay Ramsar site was not read, so this pack cannot say which parts of the island are inside the line. It says only that the island is in the site, which is what the published material says.
The two Quandamooka ILUAs are still unread, and naming the Native Title Act that registers them does not change that. See docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md B16.

No Commonwealth dollar figure touching this island was established: not a financial assistance grant share, not a ranger agreement, not a disaster activation, not a black spot round. The routes are recorded; the amounts are not.

Australia Post's community service obligation is recorded as an obligation. What mail service Minjerribah actually receives, how often, and through which outlet, was not established, and the pack contains no lever for it because no decision maker for it is recorded in the institutions list.

The Dunwich airfield is published as uncertified, so no Commonwealth aerodrome standard applies to it. There is no lever here for changing that, because the airfield operator is not in this pack's institutions list and inventing a decision maker to carry a lever would be the wrong way round.
